title: Information Reliability and Market Outcomes
authors: Chihoon Cho; Richard M. Frankel; Xiumin Martin
eligible_reason: The staggered element exists (Truth in Mileage Act enforcement years IL 1990, FL 1990, OH 1992, CA 1994, with CA untreated until 1994 as the comparison), but every reported regression is a stacked DiD: each treated state forms its own cohort with a matched control state in a +/-2-year window (IL with CA, CA with IL, OH with CA, FL with CA), estimated by OLS with cohort x year and cohort x state FE ($StateYear = i.Year##i.cohortid i.Statenum##i.cohortid), ad-level covariates (Age, Generation, Dealer, OriginalOwner, MustSell, Damage, UnverifiableDis, car-trim dummies) and time-varying state controls (change in median income, change in unemployment). Stacking, the covariates, and in Table 4 the mileage interactions all violate the rules. No unstacked state-by-year TWFE is reported.
design_notes: Data: 230428 Ad Data.dta (16,133 Toyota Corolla classified ads, hand-coded from four newspapers; Data Preparation.do keeps Repeated==0, Lines>=0, missing(Multiple), Age<=10, non-missing Price -> sample flag); 230428 State Data.xlsx (FRED income, BLS unemployment). Coverage: CA and IL 1985-1996 (May ads), OH 1990-1994 (October), FL 1988-1992 (August). Stacking (Data Preparation.do lines 222-270): for each treated state, keep that state and its designated control state for Year in [year-2, year+2), treat = State==treatstate, post = Year>=year, TIMA = treat*post, plus TIMApre2/pre1/post1/post2 relative-year dummies; append cohorts; cohortid = group(cohortname). Regressions (Test.do): reg Price_A_w ... $StateYear if sample, vce(cluster Cluster) with Cluster = group(State Year), followed by boottest wild-cluster bootstrap over Statenum Year. Table 4 Panel C: price-mileage sensitivity via MileTIMA = Mileage_w_dm*TIMA with c.Mileage_w_dm##($Cartrim $StateYear). Table 5: MileDis (mileage disclosure) on TIMA + covariates. Table 6: Price_A_w on TIMA (col 1) and TIMA MileDis MileDisTIMA (col 2). Table 7: lnCount_w (ad repetition) same structure. Table 8 / Figure 3: dynamic effects with Zero TIMApre1 TIMApost1 TIMApost2.
estimators_reported: stacked_did_ols (reg with cohort x year and cohort x state FE, ad-level and state covariates, wild-cluster bootstrap)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Enforcement years 1990 (IL, FL), 1992 (OH), 1994 (CA); only four states in the data and no never-treated state (CA is the not-yet-treated comparison).

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked design (cohort x year, cohort x state FE); ad-level covariates and time-varying state controls
specs.treatment_definition: ad placed in a treated state in or after its TIMA enforcement year (IL 1990, FL 1990, OH 1992, CA 1994)
specs.controls: Age_w_dm Gen_w_dm Dealer OrigOwn MustSell Damage NUnveriDis_w_dm Incomechange_dm Unempchange_dm
specs.cluster: Cluster = State x Year; boottest over Statenum Year
specs.notes: Table 5 (MileDis, line 156), Table 7 col 1 (lnCount_w, line 248) and Table 4 Panel C (MileTIMA interaction, line 124) share the structure; Table 6/7 col 2 add MileDis and MileDis*TIMA

specs.treatment_var: Zero TIMApre1 TIMApost1 TIMApost2 (relative to TIMA-2)

data_access: public (hand-collected newspaper ads shipped in the package; FRED and BLS state series shipped)
data_files: Data/230428 State Data.xlsx (FRED income and BLS unemployment, 1984-1997)
replication_feasible: no (no eligible specification; an unstacked state-year TWFE could be built but is not reported)
screener_notes: Article text not available; table numbers come from the do-file comments and match the abstract (32.6% price-mileage sensitivity, 23.4% disclosure, 9.7% price, 13.4% repetition). Only four states and three enforcement years; the design is stacked by construction with each treated state paired to one control state.
